newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil slips but above Friday.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil slips but above Friday.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps lost some of its early morning gains late afternoon on Monday but was still above Friday's prices despite an unexpectedly low award from India for September arrival cargoes, traders said.
"The market is hoping that the whole complex will go up because of the three cat-cracker shutdowns in Europe," one trader said.
August was last quoted at $22.50/$22.60, up slightly from Friday's $22.45/$22.55, but down from this morning's $22.60/$22.75, brokers said.
August traded earlier in the day at $21.50 compared to Friday's traded intra-day low of $22.45 after news of the low India award first filtered through the market, they said.
September also settled five cents higher with trades seen earlier in the day at $23.25 and $23.29, brokers said.

Traders said the market discounted India's low purchase of 90,000 tonnes of high-speed diesel in two cargoes for September delivery, even though it was well below the market's most conservative estimate of 200,000 tonnes on Friday.

"This is a low volume time of the year," one trader said. "But the fact that India took the much lower volume is surprising. I think they are trying to talk down the market in anticipation of some term talks."

In Europe, two catalytic converters, one at the BP/Texaco Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam and one at the BP/Mobil Coryton refinery in the U.K. were shut down on Friday due to technical problems, taking out 115,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) of capacity until the middle of next week.
In addition, Shell confirmed on Friday that the cat-cracker at its Pernis refinery has closed for an unscheduled stoppage in August followed by a scheduled maintenance of two months.
The shutdown of these two units led to August gas oil ending up $2.50 on London's International Petroleum Exchange on Friday to $171.50 per tonne.
August fuel oil was steady at $101.25/$101.75 per tonne, brokers said.
